{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"182c271d74a53139c7c2a5791867f17c601f07cf9f5414d476f7f6498953e352","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:26","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops — C.01","heading":"C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
The Driver License Compact is described as a framework for cooperation among states on licensing issues. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
The compact discussion uses the concept of one driver license and one driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Alcohol slows activity in the brain and spinal cord. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Alcohol absorbed from the stomach enters the blood and reaches the body, including the brain. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Larger amounts of alcohol produce a rising blood-alcohol level and more intense impairment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Blood Alcohol Concentration, or BAC, names the concentration of alcohol in the blood. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
The quantity of alcohol consumed is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
The length of time over which drinking occurs is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
A person's body weight is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes pure ethyl alcohol as a clear, colorless liquid with a burning taste. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
Ethyl alcohol mixes readily with other liquids, and adding water or mixer reduces its strength. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes beer as usually about five percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists wine examples at 12 or 20 percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes hard-liquor examples at about 40 to 50 percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
The handbook's comparison assigns about one-half ounce of alcohol to a 12-ounce beer, a wine serving of three to five ounces, or an 86-proof liquor serving of one and one-half ounces. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
A person may notice alcohol effects soon after drinking starts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
Alcohol effects can grow as more alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Food or milk in the stomach slows alcohol absorption. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
Coffee, a shower or exercise does not provide a way to eliminate alcohol faster and sober up sooner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
For the same alcohol amount, a heavier person will likely have a lower BAC than a lighter person because of greater blood and body-fluid volume. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A02
At a BAC of 0.08 percent, a person is impaired mentally and physically even when no outward signs are visible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A02
Some regular drinkers can conceal outward signs even at relatively high BAC levels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A03
Increasing BAC further impairs traffic judgment and decision accuracy whether or not the person looks impaired. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A03
Alcohol reduces the ability to identify, predict, decide and execute during driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A03
Alcohol-impaired vision, hearing and body-position sensing reduce a driver's ability to detect traffic hazards. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A03
An impaired driver may fix vision on one object and miss others. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A03
The handbook warns that alcohol impairment can nearly eliminate detection of people and vehicles to the side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A03
Alcohol reduces hearing and the ability to judge distance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A03
A high-BAC driver may lose body-position awareness and drift across the centerline, between lanes or off the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A03
Impaired vision, hearing and body-position sensing make predicting other drivers' actions difficult. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A03
Faulty senses, judgments and predictions undermine decisions in critical driving situations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A03
Alcohol can produce false confidence and poor judgment that contribute to bad driving decisions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A04
The simulator examples describe drink-impaired subjects choosing the wrong turn direction or accelerator instead of brake despite appearing sober. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A04
Even when a drink-impaired driver chooses the correct maneuver, execution may be slower. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A04
The handbook's braking example has a drinking driver at 55 mph travel at least 32 extra feet before applying the brakes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A04
That execution-delay example describes an added two-fifths of a second that can matter even at lower speeds. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A04
Alcohol affects inexperienced drivers more strongly than experienced drivers, and small amounts can sharply increase their errors. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A04
Beginning drinkers often show greater impairment after drinking than people with more drinking experience. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A04
Unusual weather, lighting or roads increase driving demands while alcohol reduces the ability to meet them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A04
Tiredness, anger, anxiety, emotional upset or elation may already impair a driver before alcohol reduces the ability to compensate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A04
The handbook identifies anger combined with alcohol as particularly dangerous. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: Looking sober does not establish unimpaired driving, and coffee or a shower does not provide a shortcut to sobriety.
Mnemonics: Recall index: identify, predict, decide, execute; these are the handbook's named driving tasks.
Glossary: Recall terms: blood alcohol concentration, implied consent, controlled drug, probable cause and traffic-stop cooperation.
Dynamic facts: Current compact membership, crash statistics, drug legality and present legal applicability are withheld or retained as freshness debt; no timer is presented as permission to drive.
